title.zh: 卷一百四十四 志第九十七 儀衞二
title.raw: 卷一百四十四 志第九十七 儀衞二 Volume 144 Treatises 97: Ceremonial Guards 2

sentences.zh: 儀衛二○宮中導從行幸儀衛太上皇儀衛後妃儀衛

translations.literal: Ceremonial Guards 2 ○ Palace Escorts; Touring Escorts; Retired Emperor Escorts; Consort Escorts
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial Guards 2: Palace Escorts; Touring Escorts; Retired Emperor Escorts; Consort Escorts

sentences.zh: 宮中導從之製，唐已前無聞焉。

translations.literal: As for regulations for palace escorts, nothing is heard of before the Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations governing palace escorts are not attested before the Tang dynasty.

sentences.zh: 五代漢乾祐中，始置主輦十六人，捧足一人，掌扇四人，持踏床一人，並服文綾袍、銀葉弓腳襆頭。

translations.literal: In the Qianyou era of Later Han in the Five Dynasties, there were first established sixteen palanquin bearers, one foot supporter, four fan bearers, and one footrest bearer, all wearing patterned damask robes and silver-leaf bow-foot headwraps.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianyou reign of Later Han in the Five Dynasties, the court first appointed sixteen palanquin bearers, one foot attendant, four fan bearers, and one footrest bearer, all in patterned damask robes with silver-leaf bow-foot headwraps.

sentences.zh: 尚宮一人，寶省一人，高鬢、紫衣。

translations.literal: One Director of the Palace, one of the Treasure Bureau, high side-buns and purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: One Director of the Palace and one from the Treasure Bureau, with high side-buns and purple robes.

sentences.zh: 書省二人，紫衣、弓腳襆頭。

translations.literal: Two of the Writing Bureau, purple robes and bow-foot headwraps.
translations.idiomatic: Two from the Writing Bureau in purple robes and bow-foot headwraps.

sentences.zh: 新婦二人，高鬟、青袍。

translations.literal: Two bridal attendants, high topknots and green robes.
translations.idiomatic: Two bridal attendants with high topknots and green robes.

sentences.zh: 大將二人，紫衣、弓腳襆頭。

translations.literal: Two generals, purple robes and bow-foot headwraps.
translations.idiomatic: Two generals in purple robes and bow-foot headwraps.

sentences.zh: 童子執紅絲拂二人，高鬟髻、青衣。

translations.literal: Two youths holding red-silk whisks, high topknots and green garments.
translations.idiomatic: Two youths bearing red-silk whisks, with high topknots and green garments.

sentences.zh: 執犀盤二人，帶鬅頭、黃衫。

translations.literal: Two bearing rhinoceros-horn trays, with unkempt topknots and yellow shirts.
translations.idiomatic: Two attendants carrying rhinoceros-horn trays, with topknot headwear and yellow shirts.

sentences.zh: 執翟尾二人，帶鬅頭、黃衫。

translations.literal: Two bearing pheasant tails, with unkempt topknots and yellow shirts.
translations.idiomatic: Two attendants carrying pheasant-tail plumes, with topknot headwear and yellow shirts.

sentences.zh: 雞冠二人，紫衣，分執金灌器、唾壺。

translations.literal: Two Cock's-Comb attendants in purple robes, respectively holding a gold pouring vessel and a spittoon.
translations.idiomatic: Two Cock's-Comb attendants in purple, one with a gold pouring vessel and one with a spittoon.

sentences.zh: 女冠二人，紫衣，執香爐、香盤。

translations.literal: Two female Daoist attendants in purple robes, holding an incense burner and an incense tray.
translations.idiomatic: Two female Daoist attendants in purple, bearing an incense burner and an incense tray.

sentences.zh: 分左右以次奉引。

translations.literal: They were divided left and right to lead in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: They were arrayed left and right to lead the procession in order.

sentences.zh: 太宗太平興國初，增主輦二十四人，改服高腳襆頭；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo under Emperor Taizong, twenty-four palanquin bearers were added, and dress was changed to high-foot headwraps;
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiping Xingguo era under Emperor Taizong, twenty-four palanquin bearers were added and their headwear was changed to high-foot wraps;

sentences.zh: 輦頭一人，衣紫繡袍，持金塗銀仗以督領之。

translations.literal: one palanquin director in a purple embroidered robe, holding a gold-plated silver staff to supervise them.
translations.idiomatic: one palanquin director in a purple embroidered robe, bearing a gold-plated silver staff to command them.

sentences.zh: 奉珍珠、七寶、翠毛華樹二人，衣緋袍；

translations.literal: two bearing pearl, seven-treasure, and kingfisher-feather ornamental trees, in scarlet robes;
translations.idiomatic: Two attendants carrying pearl, seven-treasure, and kingfisher-feather ornamental trees, in scarlet robes;

sentences.zh: 奉金寶山二人，衣綠繡袍；

translations.literal: two bearing gold treasure mountains, in green embroidered robes;
translations.idiomatic: two bearing gold treasure mountains, in green embroidered robes;

sentences.zh: 奉龍腦合二人，衣緋銷金袍，並高腳襆頭。

translations.literal: two bearing camphor caskets, in scarlet gold-thread brocade robes, all with high-foot headwraps.
translations.idiomatic: two carrying camphor caskets, in scarlet gold-thread brocade robes, all wearing high-foot headwraps.

sentences.zh: 執拂翟四人，鬅頭、衣黃繡袍。

translations.literal: four holding pheasant-tail whisks, with topknots and yellow embroidered robes.
translations.idiomatic: Four attendants with pheasant-tail whisks, topknot headwear, and yellow embroidered robes.

sentences.zh: 舊衣綾袍、紫衣者，悉易以銷金及繡。

translations.literal: Those who formerly wore damask robes and purple garments were all changed to gold-thread brocade and embroidery.
translations.idiomatic: Former damask robes and purple garments were all replaced with gold-thread brocade and embroidery.

sentences.zh: 復增司薄一人，內省一人，司儀一人，司給一人，皆分左右前導，凡一十七行。

translations.literal: There were further added one registrar, one inner secretariat officer, one master of ceremonies, and one supply officer, all divided left and right to lead ahead, seventeen rows in all.
translations.idiomatic: The court also added one registrar, one inner secretariat officer, one master of ceremonies, and one supply officer, each posted left and right to lead ahead—a total of seventeen rows.

sentences.zh: 每正、至禦殿，祀郊廟，步輦出入至長春殿用之。

translations.literal: Whenever at the winter and summer solstices the emperor attended the hall, sacrificed at the suburban altars and ancestral temples, or the walking palanquin entered and left as far as Ever-Spring Hall, this was used.
translations.idiomatic: This escort was used whenever the emperor attended court at the solstices, performed suburban and temple sacrifices, or the walking palanquin passed in and out as far as Ever-Spring Hall.

sentences.zh: 其乘輦，則屈右足、垂左足而憑幾，蓋唐製也。

translations.literal: When riding the palanquin, one bent the right foot, let the left foot hang down, and leaned on an armrest—this was Tang practice.
translations.idiomatic: When seated in the palanquin, the rider bent the right leg, let the left foot hang down, and rested on an armrest—a Tang custom.

sentences.zh: 真宗時，加四面內官周衛。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Zhenzong, inner palace officials were added on all four sides as a surrounding guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhenzong, inner palace officials were posted on all four sides as a surrounding guard.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符三年，內出繪圖以示宰相。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu, a painted diagram was issued from within the palace to show the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu, the palace issued a painted diagram for the chief ministers to review.

sentences.zh: 行幸儀衛。

translations.literal: Touring ceremonial guards.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial Guards for Imperial Tours.

sentences.zh: 宋初，三駕皆以待禮事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, all three imperial progresses were reserved for ritual occasions.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song, all three grades of imperial procession were reserved for ritual occasions.

sentences.zh: 車駕近出，止用常從以行。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage went out on nearby excursions, only the regular escort was used to travel.
translations.idiomatic: For nearby outings, the imperial carriage relied only on the regular escort.

sentences.zh: 其舊儀，殿前司隨駕馬隊，凡諸班直內，殿前指揮使全班祗應：左班七十六人，二十四人在駕前左邊引駕，五十二人作兩隊隨駕；

translations.literal: According to the old regulations, the Bureau of the Palatial Guard's escort cavalry: among all the duty shifts within the various companies, the Palatial Guard commanders' full company attended—left company seventy-six men, twenty-four on the left before the carriage to lead it, fifty-two in two squads following the carriage;
translations.idiomatic: Under the old regulations, the Palatial Guard's escort cavalry: among all duty shifts, the commanders' full company attended—the left company numbered seventy-six, with twenty-four on the left before the carriage to lead it and fifty-two in two squads following;

sentences.zh: 右班七十七人，二十四人在駕前右邊引駕，五十三人在駕後作兩隊隨駕，二十七人第一隊，二十六人第二隊。

translations.literal: right company seventy-seven men, twenty-four on the right before the carriage to lead it, fifty-three behind the carriage in two squads following, twenty-seven in the first squad and twenty-six in the second.
translations.idiomatic: the right company numbered seventy-seven, with twenty-four on the right before the carriage to lead it and fifty-three behind in two squads—twenty-seven in the first and twenty-six in the second.

sentences.zh: 內殿直五十四人，散員六十四人，散指揮六十四人，散都頭五十四人，散祗候五十四人，金槍五十四人，茶酒班祗應殿侍百五十七人，東第二班長入祗候殿侍十八人，駕後動樂三十一人，馬隊弩手分東西八十五人，招箭班三十五人，散直百七人，鈞容直三百二十人，禦龍直百四十二人，禦龍骨朵子直二百二十人，並全班祗應。

translations.literal: Inner Hall Direct fifty-four, scattered members sixty-four, scattered commanders sixty-four, scattered squad leaders fifty-four, scattered attendants fifty-four, golden spears fifty-four, tea-and-wine shift palace attendants one hundred fifty-seven, eastern second company senior palace attendants eighteen, post-carriage ceremonial music thirty-one, cavalry crossbowmen divided east and west eighty-five, arrow-recruitment company thirty-five, scattered direct one hundred seven, Imperial Music Direct three hundred twenty, Imperial Dragon Direct one hundred forty-two, Imperial Dragon mace Direct two hundred twenty—all full companies attending.
translations.idiomatic: Also attending in full companies were: Inner Hall Direct (54), scattered members (64), scattered commanders (64), scattered squad leaders (54), scattered attendants (54), golden spears (54), tea-and-wine shift palace attendants (157), eastern second company senior palace attendants (18), post-carriage ceremonial music (31), cavalry crossbowmen east and west (85), arrow-recruitment company (35), scattered direct (107), Imperial Music Direct (320), Imperial Dragon Direct (142), and Imperial Dragon mace Direct (220).

sentences.zh: 禦龍弓箭直百三十三人，禦龍弩直百三十三人，寬衣天武指揮二百一十六人。

translations.literal: Imperial Dragon bow Direct one hundred thirty-three, Imperial Dragon crossbow Direct one hundred thirty-three, broad-garment Heavenly Martial command two hundred sixteen.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Dragon bow Direct (133), Imperial Dragon crossbow Direct (133), and broad-garment Heavenly Martial command (216).

sentences.zh: （各有都虞候、指揮使、員僚。）〉

translations.literal: (Each had a chief adjutant, commander, and staff officers.)
translations.idiomatic: (Each unit had a chief adjutant, commander, and staff officers.)

sentences.zh: 若隨駕不使馬隊，即減內殿直、散員、散指揮、散都頭、散祗候、金槍等直，仍減東西班馬隊弩手八十五人，餘並同上。

translations.literal: If the escort did not employ the cavalry squad, then Inner Hall Direct, scattered members, scattered commanders, scattered squad leaders, scattered attendants, golden spears, and the like were reduced, and the east and west cavalry crossbowmen of eighty-five were also reduced; the rest was as above.
translations.idiomatic: When the escort did not use the cavalry squad, Inner Hall Direct and the scattered companies and golden spears were omitted, along with the eighty-five east-west cavalry crossbowmen; all else followed the same arrangement.

sentences.zh: 凡皇城司隨駕人數：崇政殿祗應親從四指揮共二百五十二人，執擎骨朵，充禁衛；

translations.literal: As for the Imperial City Bureau personnel accompanying the carriage: four companies of Chongzheng Hall attending personal followers, two hundred fifty-two in all, holding maces, serving as inner guard;
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial City Bureau's escort comprised four companies of Chongzheng Hall personal followers (252 men), bearing maces as the inner guard;

sentences.zh: 崇政殿門外快行、祗候、親從第四指揮五十四人；

translations.literal: outside Chongzheng Hall, fast runners, attendants, and the fourth company of personal followers, fifty-four men;
translations.idiomatic: outside Chongzheng Hall, fast runners, attendants, and the fourth personal-follower company (54 men);

sentences.zh: 車駕導從、兩壁隨行親從親事官共九十六人，並於駕前先行，行幸所到之處，充行宮司把門、灑掃祗應。

translations.literal: carriage escorts and personal-follower attendants of both flanks traveling along, ninety-six in all, all going ahead before the carriage; wherever the tour arrived, they served as temporary palace gatekeepers and sweepers.
translations.idiomatic: ninety-six carriage escorts and flank personal-follower attendants marched ahead of the carriage; at each stop they served as temporary gatekeepers and sweepers for the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: （各有正副都頭、節級、十將。）〉

translations.literal: (Each had chief and deputy squad leaders, section chiefs, and decurions.)
translations.idiomatic: (Each unit had chief and deputy squad leaders, section chiefs, and decurions.)

sentences.zh: 尚書兵部供黃麾仗內法物：罕罼各一。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War of the Secretariat supplied ritual objects within the yellow-banner guard: one canopy and one parasol each.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat's Ministry of War furnished ritual objects for the yellow-banner guard: one canopy and one parasol apiece.

sentences.zh: 五色繡氅子並龍頭竿掛，第一，青繡孔雀氅；

translations.literal: Five-colored embroidered pennants with dragon-head pole mounts: first, green embroidered peacock pennant;
translations.idiomatic: Five-colored embroidered pennants on dragon-head poles: first, a green embroidered peacock pennant;

sentences.zh: 第二，緋繡鳳氅；

translations.literal: second, scarlet embroidered phoenix pennant;
translations.idiomatic: second, a scarlet embroidered phoenix pennant;

sentences.zh: 第三，青繡孔雀氅；

translations.literal: third, green embroidered peacock pennant;
translations.idiomatic: third, a green embroidered peacock pennant;

sentences.zh: 第四，皂繡鵝氅；

translations.literal: fourth, black embroidered goose pennant;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, a black embroidered goose pennant;

sentences.zh: 第五，白繡鵝氅；

translations.literal: fifth, white embroidered goose pennant;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, a white embroidered goose pennant;

sentences.zh: 第六，黃繡雞氅。

translations.literal: sixth, yellow embroidered rooster pennant.
translations.idiomatic: sixth, a yellow embroidered rooster pennant.

sentences.zh: 又六軍儀仗司供儀仗法物，內獅子旗四口，充門旗二口，各一人執，分左右；

translations.literal: The Six Armies Ceremonial Guard Bureau also supplied ceremonial objects, including four lion flags; two served as gate flags, each with one bearer, divided left and right;
translations.idiomatic: The Six Armies Ceremonial Guard Bureau also supplied ceremonial objects, including four lion flags—two as gate flags, each borne by one man, left and right;

sentences.zh: 二口各十人執扯，分左右，扯人執弓箭。

translations.literal: two flags each with ten men to hold and draw them, left and right; the drawers bore bows and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: two flags each with ten men to trail them, left and right, the trail-bearers armed with bows and arrows.

sentences.zh: 又左金吾引駕仗供牙門旗十四口，十口開五門，每門二口，每口一人執二人夾，計三十人，並騎，夾人執弓箭。

translations.literal: The Left Golden Crow escort guard also supplied fourteen gate flags; ten opened five gates, two flags per gate, one bearer and two flanking men per flag, thirty men in all, all mounted; the flankers bore bows and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Golden Crow escort guard furnished fourteen gate flags—ten forming five gates of two flags each, with one bearer and two flankers per flag (thirty mounted men in all), the flankers armed with bows and arrows.

sentences.zh: 監門校尉二十人，每門四人，並帶儀刀，騎。

translations.literal: Twenty gate-wardens, four per gate, all wearing ceremonial swords, mounted.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty gate-wardens (four per gate), mounted and wearing ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 二口係前步甲第七隊前，二口係前部黃麾第一隊前，二口係後部黃麾第一隊前，二口係後步甲第一隊前，二口係後步甲第七隊前。

translations.literal: Two flags were placed before the front infantry seventh squad, two before the front yellow-banner first squad, two before the rear yellow-banner first squad, two before the rear infantry first squad, and two before the rear infantry seventh squad.
translations.idiomatic: Two flags stood before the front infantry seventh squad, two before the front yellow-banner first squad, two before the rear yellow-banner first squad, two before the rear infantry first squad, and two before the rear infantry seventh squad.

sentences.zh: 四口開二門，每門二口，每口一人執二人夾，計十二人，並騎。

translations.literal: Four flags opened two gates, two flags per gate, one bearer and two flankers per flag, twelve men in all, all mounted.
translations.idiomatic: Four flags formed two gates of two flags each, with one bearer and two flankers per flag—twelve mounted men in all.

sentences.zh: 監門校尉六人，並帶儀刀，騎。

translations.literal: Six gate-wardens, all wearing ceremonial swords, mounted.
translations.idiomatic: Six gate-wardens, mounted and wearing ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 二口係兵部班劍儀刀隊後，二口係真武隊前。

translations.literal: Two flags were placed behind the Ministry of War sword-and-ceremonial-blade squad, and two before the True Martial squad.
translations.idiomatic: Two flags followed the Ministry of War sword-and-ceremonial-blade squad, and two preceded the True Martial squad.

sentences.zh: 又右金吾引駕仗供牙門旗十四口，製同左仗。

translations.literal: The Right Golden Crow escort guard also supplied fourteen gate flags, made the same as the left guard.
translations.idiomatic: The Right Golden Crow escort guard also furnished fourteen gate flags, identical to those on the left.

sentences.zh: 仁宗康定元年，參知政事宋庠言：“車駕行幸，非郊廟大禮具陳鹵薄外，其常日導從，惟前有駕頭，後擁傘扇而已，殊無禮典所載公卿奉引之盛。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangding under Emperor Renzong, Vice Grand Councilor Song Qi said: "When the imperial carriage tours, apart from suburban and temple great rites with the full guard of honor deployed, on ordinary days the escort has only the carriage leader before and umbrellas and fans behind—far from the grandeur of dukes and ministers leading as recorded in ritual canon.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kangding, Vice Grand Councilor Song Qi said: "On imperial tours, apart from suburban and temple rites when the full guard of honor is deployed, the everyday escort amounts to a carriage leader ahead and umbrellas and fans behind—nothing like the grand procession of dukes and ministers leading the way described in the ritual canon.

sentences.zh: 其侍從及百司官屬，下至廝役，皆雜行道中。

translations.literal: Attendants and officials of the hundred offices, down to menials, all mingle in the roadway.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants and officials of every bureau, down to menials, all mingle in the roadway.

sentences.zh: 步輦之後，但以親事官百餘人執楇以殿，謂之禁衛。

translations.literal: Behind the walking palanquin, only a hundred-odd personal attendants holding clubs bring up the rear—this is called the inner guard.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the walking palanquin, a mere hundred-odd personal attendants with clubs bring up the rear—this alone is called the inner guard.

sentences.zh: 諸班勁騎，頗與乘輿相遠；

translations.literal: The crack cavalry of the various companies are quite far from the imperial carriage;
translations.idiomatic: The elite cavalry of the various companies stand quite far from the imperial carriage;

sentences.zh: 士庶觀者，率隨扈從之人，夾道馳走，喧呼不禁。

translations.literal: Commoners watching generally follow the escort personnel, running along both sides of the road with shouts unchecked.
translations.idiomatic: Spectators commonly chase alongside the escort, running down both sides of the road with unchecked shouting.

sentences.zh: 所過旗亭市樓，垂簾外蔽，士民馮高下瞰，莫為嚴憚。

translations.literal: At wine pavilions and market towers along the route, curtains hung outward as screens; gentry and commoners leaned over high and low to look down, showing no awe.
translations.idiomatic: At wine pavilions and market towers along the route, curtains hung outward; gentry and commoners peered down from every vantage without the least restraint.

sentences.zh: 邏司街使，恬不嗬止。

translations.literal: Patrol officers and street commissioners calmly did not shout to stop them.
translations.idiomatic: Patrol officers and street commissioners made no effort to stop them.

sentences.zh: 威令弛闕，玩習為常。

translations.literal: Authority and orders were lax and deficient; lax practice had become routine.
translations.idiomatic: Authority had grown slack, and disorder had become routine.

sentences.zh: 非所謂旄頭先驅，清道後行之慎也。

translations.literal: This is not what is meant by the battle-ax banner going ahead as vanguard and clearing the road before the rear guard proceeds with caution.
translations.idiomatic: This falls far short of the vigilance implied when the vanguard clears the road before the rear guard follows.

sentences.zh: 且自黃帝以神功盛德，猶假師兵營衛，則防微禦變，古今一體。

translations.literal: Moreover, from the Yellow Emperor onward, despite divine merit and sagely virtue, troops were still borrowed for camp guards—thus guarding against the subtle and warding off change is one principle in ancient and modern times alike.
translations.idiomatic: Even the Yellow Emperor, for all his divine merit, still relied on troops for camp guards—guarding against small dangers is the same principle in every age.

sentences.zh: 案漢魏以降，有大駕、小駕之儀。

translations.literal: Examining from Han and Wei downward, there were ceremonies for the great progress and the small progress.
translations.idiomatic: From Han and Wei onward, courts distinguished great and small imperial progresses.

sentences.zh: 至唐又分殿中諸衛、黃麾等仗，名數次序，各有施設。

translations.literal: By Tang times there were further divided the various guards of the palace interior, yellow-banner guards, and the like, each with titles, numbers, sequence, and its own deployment.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang, palace guards, yellow-banner units, and the like were further subdivided, each with its own titles, numbers, order, and deployment.

sentences.zh: 國朝承五姓荒殘之弊，事從簡略，每鳴鑾遊豫，盡去戈戟、旌旗之製，儀衛寡薄，頗同藩鎮。

translations.literal: Our dynasty inherited the ruin left by the Five Dynasties; affairs followed simplicity. Whenever the bell sounded for imperial excursions, halberds, spears, and banner regalia were entirely removed; ceremonial guards were thin, much like a military governor's entourage.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty inherited the devastation of the Five Dynasties and kept affairs simple. On every imperial outing the court stripped away halberds, spears, and banners; the guard was meager, scarcely distinguishable from a regional commander's train.

sentences.zh: 此皆制度放失，憚於改作之咎。

translations.literal: All this was because institutions had been let slip, with fear of the blame for reform.
translations.idiomatic: All of this reflected institutions left to lapse and a fear of being blamed for reform.

sentences.zh: 宜委一二博學近臣，討繹前代儀注及鹵薄令，以乘輿常時出入之儀，比之三駕諸仗，酌取其中，稍增儀物，具嚴法禁，以示尊極，以防未然。

translations.literal: It is fitting to commission one or two learned officials close at hand to study former dynasties' ritual regulations and guard-of-honor statutes, taking the imperial carriage's ordinary coming-and-going ceremony, comparing it with the three progresses' various guards, selecting from among them, slightly increasing ceremonial objects, fully providing strict laws and prohibitions, to display supreme dignity and guard against what has not yet happened.
translations.idiomatic: The court should commission one or two learned officials nearby to review earlier dynasties' ritual codes and guard-of-honor statutes, compare the emperor's routine outings with the three grades of procession, adopt what fits, add ceremonial objects, enforce strict prohibitions, display imperial dignity, and forestall trouble before it arises.

sentences.zh: 革去因循，其在今日。

translations.literal: To cast off routine procrastination—the time is today.
translations.idiomatic: To break free of entrenched habit—there is no better time than now.

sentences.zh: ”詔太常禮院與兩製詳定，參以舊儀，別加新製。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered the Directorate of Ritual of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Hanlin Academy to deliberate in detail, taking the old regulations as reference and separately adding new provisions.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' Directorate of Ritual and the Hanlin Academy to deliberate in detail, drawing on old regulations while adding new provisions.

sentences.zh: 兩製同禮官議，略準小駕制度，添清道馬、罕罼、旗氅等物。

translations.literal: The Hanlin Academy together with ritual officials deliberated, roughly following the small-progress system, adding road-clearing horses, canopy and parasol, flags and pennants, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: The Hanlin Academy and ritual officials agreed to follow the small-progress model roughly, adding road-clearing horses, canopy and parasol, flags, pennants, and similar items.

sentences.zh: 別為常行禁衛儀，加清道馬百匹，並帶器械，分五行，行二十人。

translations.literal: A separate routine inner-guard ceremony was established, adding one hundred road-clearing horses, all bearing weapons, divided into five rows of twenty men each.
translations.idiomatic: They established a separate ceremony for the routine inner guard, adding one hundred road-clearing horses armed with weapons, in five rows of twenty.

sentences.zh: （請下殿前司，於諸班內差。）〉

translations.literal: (It is requested that the Bureau of the Palatial Guard be ordered to detail men from among the various companies.)
translations.idiomatic: (The Palatial Guard should detail men from the various companies.)

sentences.zh: 罕罼各一，分左右，並騎。

translations.literal: One canopy and one parasol each, divided left and right, all mounted.
translations.idiomatic: One canopy and one parasol apiece, left and right, all mounted.

sentences.zh: 牙門旗前後各四，分左右，並騎。

translations.literal: Four gate flags before and four behind, divided left and right, all mounted.
translations.idiomatic: Four gate flags before and four behind, left and right, all mounted.

sentences.zh: 緋繡鳳氅二十四，分左右，並騎。

translations.literal: Twenty-four scarlet embroidered phoenix pennants, divided left and right, all mounted.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-four scarlet embroidered phoenix pennants, left and right, all mounted.

sentences.zh: （以上請下殿前司，於諸班內差充。）〉

translations.literal: (For all the above, it is requested that the Bureau of the Palatial Guard be ordered to detail men from among the various companies to fill the posts.)
translations.idiomatic: (For all the above, the Palatial Guard should detail men from the various companies.)

sentences.zh: 雉扇十二，分左右。

translations.literal: Twelve pheasant-tail fans, divided left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve pheasant-tail fans, left and right.

sentences.zh: （請於親從官內差充。）〉

translations.literal: (It is requested that men be detailed from among the personal followers to fill the posts.)
translations.idiomatic: (Men should be detailed from the personal followers.)

sentences.zh: 以上新添百六十二人。

translations.literal: The above newly added one hundred sixty-two men.
translations.idiomatic: These additions came to one hundred sixty-two men.

sentences.zh: 凡天武官舊二百一十六人，空行，今添執哥舒，為一重。

translations.literal: The Heavenly Martial officials formerly numbered two hundred sixteen, marching empty-handed; now they are to hold geku shields, forming one layer.
translations.idiomatic: The Heavenly Martial guard formerly numbered two hundred sixteen and marched empty-handed; they were now to carry geku shields as one layer.

sentences.zh: 親從官舊百四十五人，今添百五十五人，通為三百人，為一重。

translations.literal: Personal followers formerly one hundred forty-five; now one hundred fifty-five are added, three hundred in all, forming one layer.
translations.idiomatic: Personal followers formerly numbered one hundred forty-five; with one hundred fifty-five added, they totaled three hundred as one layer.

sentences.zh: 殿前指揮使舊四十八人，今添百五十二人，通為二百人，或於近上諸班相兼差充，並騎，為一重。

translations.literal: Palatial Guard commanders formerly forty-eight; now one hundred fifty-two are added, two hundred in all, or concurrently detailed from the senior companies nearby, all mounted, forming one layer.
translations.idiomatic: Palatial Guard commanders formerly numbered forty-eight; with one hundred fifty-two added they totaled two hundred, some concurrently drawn from senior companies, all mounted as one layer.

sentences.zh: 以上因舊人數添。

translations.literal: The above augmented the former numbers.
translations.idiomatic: The above augmented existing personnel.

sentences.zh: （舊四百九人，新添三百七人，共七百一十六人。）〉

translations.literal: (Formerly four hundred nine men; newly added three hundred seven; seven hundred sixteen in all.)
translations.idiomatic: (Formerly 409 men; 307 added; 716 in all.)

sentences.zh: 凡駕前殿前指揮使、親從官為二重，左右相對，各開二門，約二丈，每門並差人員二人押當。

translations.literal: Before the carriage, Palatial Guard commanders and personal followers formed two layers, facing each other left and right, each opening two gates about two zhang apart; at each gate two men were detailed to hold position.
translations.idiomatic: Before the carriage, Palatial Guard commanders and personal followers formed two facing ranks, each opening two gates roughly two zhang apart, with two men posted at each gate.

sentences.zh: 第一門與通事舍人相對，第二門與閣門使相對。

translations.literal: The first gate faced the Communications Attendants; the second gate faced the Gate Commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: The first gate faced the Communications Attendants; the second faced the Gate Commissioners.

sentences.zh: 每有臣僚迎駕起居，並令中道候起居畢，於左右門出。

translations.literal: Whenever officials came to greet the carriage and perform obeisance, all were ordered to wait in the central roadway until obeisance was finished, then exit through the left or right gate.
translations.idiomatic: When officials came to greet the carriage, they waited in the central roadway until obeisance was complete, then exited through the left or right gate.

sentences.zh: 其諸色人止令於牙門旗前道傍起居，不得便入禁衛中。

translations.literal: Persons of various ranks were only ordered to perform obeisance by the roadside before the gate flags and were not permitted to enter the inner guard zone.
translations.idiomatic: Persons of every rank were permitted obeisance only by the roadside before the gate flags and could not enter the inner guard.

sentences.zh: （每門外重，令殿前指揮使執旗二面以表門，用轉光錯彩旗，通上計五重，皆掩後團轉。）〉

translations.literal: (Outside each gate layer, Palatial Guard commanders were ordered to hold two flags to mark the gate, using iridescent multicolored flags; counting upward there were five layers in all, all wheeling behind in a closed circle.)
translations.idiomatic: (Outside each gate, commanders bore two iridescent multicolored flags to mark it; five layers in all wheeled behind in a closed circle.)

sentences.zh: 凡百司祗應人於禁衛內無執掌者，及隨駕臣僚除合將入禁衛隨從人數外，餘並令於殿前指揮使行外左右前後行。

translations.literal: All attendants of the hundred offices who had no duty within the inner guard, and accompanying officials apart from those permitted to enter the inner guard with their allotted followers, were all ordered to march outside the Palatial Guard commanders' ranks, left, right, before, and behind.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants of every bureau without duties inside the inner guard, and accompanying officials beyond those permitted escorts, were to march outside the commanders' ranks on every side.

sentences.zh: 凡前牙門旗以後，後牙門旗以前，屬禁衛中，不得輒入。

translations.literal: From the front gate flags rearward to before the rear gate flags belonged to the inner guard; no one might enter casually.
translations.idiomatic: The zone from the front gate flags to the rear gate flags was inner guard territory; no unauthorized entry was permitted.

sentences.zh: 凡中書、樞密院臣僚，並於從內第三重寬衣天武內行馬；

translations.literal: In general, officials of the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs all rode on horseback within the third layer inward of the escort, among the broad-garment Heavenly Martial guard;
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs officials rode within the escort's third inner layer, among the broad-garment Heavenly Martial guard.

sentences.zh: 其餘隨駕文武臣僚，並在從內第四重殿前指揮使內，分左右依官位行馬。

translations.literal: The remaining civil and military officials accompanying the carriage were all within the fourth layer inward among the Palatial Guard commanders, divided left and right according to official rank to ride on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Other accompanying civil and military officials rode within the escort's fourth inner layer among the Palatial Guard commanders, arrayed left and right by rank.

sentences.zh: 凡車駕經曆去處，若有樓閣，並不得垂簾障蔽，及止絕士庶不許臨高瞰下，止於街兩傍立觀，即不得夾路喧呼馳走。

translations.literal: Wherever the imperial carriage passed, if there were towers or pavilions, hanging curtains to obstruct view was forbidden altogether, and commoners were barred from looking down from heights; they could only stand and watch on both sides of the street, and shouting or running along the road was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever the imperial procession passed, buildings could not hang curtains to block the view; commoners were forbidden to look down from heights and had to watch from the sides of the street only, without shouting or running along the road.

sentences.zh: （前牙門以前，後牙門以後，不在此限。）〉

translations.literal: (Before the front gate flags and after the rear gate flags were not subject to this restriction.)
translations.idiomatic: (This restriction did not apply before the front gate flags or after the rear gate flags.)

sentences.zh: 凡車駕未出皇城門，宣德、左右掖、東華、拱宸門及已至所幸處，即自有門禁，不用牙門旗約束。

translations.literal: Whenever the imperial carriage had not yet left the Imperial City gates—the Xuande, Left and Right Flanking, Donghua, and Gongchen gates—or had already reached the place favored by the emperor, they had their own gate controls and did not require regulation by gate flags.
translations.idiomatic: Before the imperial procession left the Imperial City, or once it reached its destination, existing gate controls at the Xuande, Left and Right Flanking, Donghua, and Gongchen gates applied; gate flags were not needed.

sentences.zh: 凡車駕已在道，前牙門旗雖行，後牙門旗未行，除止絕閑雜行人外，其隨駕臣僚官司人等，並依常例，次第赴合隨從及行馬去處。

translations.literal: Whenever the imperial carriage was already on the road, though the front gate flags had moved but the rear gate flags had not, apart from stopping idle and miscellaneous pedestrians, accompanying officials and bureau personnel all according to routine proceeded in order to the places designated for following and riding.
translations.idiomatic: When the procession was underway, even if the front gate flags had moved but the rear had not, accompanying officials and bureau personnel still followed routine and proceeded in order to their assigned escort positions—only casual pedestrians were barred.

sentences.zh: 凡前牙門旗在清道馬後約十步已來，後牙門旗在駕後殿前指揮使之後。

translations.literal: In general, the front gate flags followed about ten paces behind the road-clearing horses; the rear gate flags followed behind the Palatial Guard commanders at the rear of the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The front gate flags marched roughly ten paces behind the road-clearing horses; the rear gate flags followed behind the Palatial Guard commanders at the rear of the procession.

sentences.zh: 凡街巷寬闊處，儀衛並依新圖排列。

translations.literal: In all broad streets and lanes, the ceremonial guards were all arranged according to the new diagram.
translations.idiomatic: On wide streets and lanes, ceremonial guards were arranged according to the new diagram.

sentences.zh: 如遇窄狹街巷，禁衛止用親從官二重，禦龍直二重，雉扇隨輦。

translations.literal: If narrow streets and lanes were encountered, the inner guard used only two layers of personal followers, two layers of Imperial Dragon Direct, and pheasant-tail fans accompanying the palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: In narrow streets, the inner guard was reduced to two layers of personal followers and two layers of Imperial Dragon Direct, with pheasant-tail fans accompanying the palanquin.

sentences.zh: 其殿前指揮使、天武官，並權分於駕前後隨行。

translations.literal: The Palatial Guard commanders and Heavenly Martial officers were all temporarily divided to follow before and after the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Palatial Guard commanders and Heavenly Martial officers were temporarily split to escort before and after the carriage.

sentences.zh: 後至寬闊處，乘輿徐行，儀仗依舊排列。

translations.literal: When they later reached broad places, the palanquin moved slowly and the ceremonial regalia was arranged as before.
translations.idiomatic: Once they reached open ground again, the palanquin slowed and the full ceremonial array was restored.

sentences.zh: 或駕幸園苑、宮觀、寺院並臣僚宅，即清道馬、儀仗、殿前指揮使、天武官更不入，惟於外排立。

translations.literal: Or when the carriage visited gardens, palaces, temples, monasteries, and officials' residences, the road-clearing horses, ceremonial regalia, Palatial Guard commanders, and Heavenly Martial officers no longer entered but were only arrayed outside.
translations.idiomatic: When visiting gardens, palaces, temples, monasteries, or officials' residences, road-clearing horses, ceremonial regalia, Palatial Guard commanders, and Heavenly Martial officers did not enter but were posted outside only.

sentences.zh: 其隨駕臣僚及諸司人，自依常例隨從，候駕行，依次排列。

translations.literal: The accompanying officials and personnel of the various bureaus themselves followed according to routine, waited for the carriage to move, and arranged themselves in order.
translations.idiomatic: Accompanying officials and bureau personnel followed routine, waiting for the carriage to move before falling into order.

sentences.zh: 或臣僚宅在巷內，前去不通人行處，其儀仗、殿前指揮使等，各於巷口排立，止絕行人，餘並如故。

translations.literal: Or if an official's residence was inside an alley where passage ahead was blocked to pedestrians, the ceremonial regalia, Palatial Guard commanders, and the like each were arrayed at the alley mouth to stop pedestrians; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: If an official's residence lay down an impassable alley, ceremonial guards and Palatial Guard commanders were posted at the alley mouth to bar pedestrians; everything else followed the usual practice.

sentences.zh: 時詳定閱習既畢，或言新製嚴密，慮違犯者眾，因不果行。

translations.literal: At the time, when the detailed review and rehearsal was completed, some said the new regulations were strict and they feared many would violate them, and so they were not put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: After the detailed review and rehearsal was completed, some argued the new regulations were too strict and would provoke widespread violations, so the plan was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐六年，先是，幸睦親宅，抱駕頭內臣墜馬，壞駕頭。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiayou, earlier when visiting the Residence of Amicable Kinship, an inner attendant holding the carriage head fell from his horse and damaged the carriage head.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiayou 6, during an earlier visit to the Residence of Amicable Kinship, an inner attendant supporting the carriage head fell from his horse and broke it.

sentences.zh: 太常禮院、閣門及整肅禁衛所請自今車駕出，以閣門祗候並內臣各二員，分駕頭左右扇筤後編攔，仍以皇城司親從官二十人隨之。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Gate, and the Office for Regulating the Inner Guard requested that from now on when the imperial carriage went out, two Gate Attendants and two inner attendants each should be placed to block and flank behind the left and right fan racks of the carriage head, with twenty personal followers of the Imperial City Command still following.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices, the Gate, and the Office for Regulating the Inner Guard requested that henceforth when the imperial carriage departed, two Gate Attendants and two inner attendants be posted behind the left and right fan racks of the carriage head to flank and block, accompanied by twenty Imperial City personal followers.

sentences.zh: 哲宗紹聖二年，詔：車駕行幸儀衛，駕後東西班殿侍馬兩隊，撥充駕前編攔，分兩壁行於前引行門之前，隨身器械，各別給銀骨朵一。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaosheng under Emperor Zhezong, an edict stated: for ceremonial guards on imperial tours, the two mounted Palace Attendant companies of the east and west rear escort were reassigned as front blocking escorts, marching in two walls before the forward gate guides, each separately given one silver geku.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaosheng 2 under Emperor Zhezong, an edict ordered that the two rear escort companies of east and west Palace Attendants be reassigned as front blocking escorts, marching in two flanks before the forward gate guides, each man issued a silver geku.

sentences.zh: 駕後馬隊、殿前指揮使馬，以百人分四隊。

translations.literal: The rear escort horse companies and Palatial Guard commanders' horses, one hundred men divided into four companies.
translations.idiomatic: The rear horse escort and Palatial Guard cavalry—one hundred men divided into four companies.

sentences.zh: 不足，據人數均差，仍別差人員六人。

translations.literal: If insufficient, men were assigned evenly according to numbers; six officers were additionally detailed.
translations.idiomatic: If numbers fell short, men were assigned evenly; six officers were additionally detailed.

sentences.zh: 內殿直、散員、散指揮、散都頭、散祗候，並增作一百四人，分四隊，內人員各四人。

translations.literal: Inner Palace Direct, scattered members, scattered commanders, scattered company heads, and scattered attendants were all increased to one hundred four men, divided into four companies, with four officers in each.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Palace Direct, scattered members, scattered commanders, scattered company heads, and scattered attendants were increased to 104 men in four companies, four officers each.

sentences.zh: 金槍班添一隊，作七十八人，內人員三人。

translations.literal: The golden spear company added one company, totaling seventy-eight men, with three officers within.
translations.idiomatic: The golden spear company gained one additional squad—78 men with three officers.

sentences.zh: 弩手班添兩隊，充填撥過東西班殿侍馬兩隊。

translations.literal: The crossbowmen companies added two companies to fill the posts vacated by the reassigned east and west Palace Attendant mounted companies.
translations.idiomatic: Two crossbowmen squads were added to fill the gap left by the reassigned east and west Palace Attendant companies.

sentences.zh: 禁衛禦龍直、弓箭直、弩直、長行，仍各添給銀骨朵。

translations.literal: Among the inner guard, Imperial Dragon Direct, bow Direct, crossbow Direct, and rank-and-file still each additionally received silver geku.
translations.idiomatic: Within the inner guard, Imperial Dragon Direct, bow Direct, crossbow Direct, and rank-and-file each received silver geku as well.

sentences.zh: 禁衛外，添差編攔天武人員、長行共二百人，揀選有行止舊人充，出入止於宣德門外，至行在所，即止於行宮門外。

translations.literal: Outside the inner guard, blocking Heavenly Martial officers and rank-and-file totaling two hundred were additionally assigned, selected from men of good conduct with prior service; on departure they stopped outside the Xuande Gate, and upon reaching the traveling palace they stopped outside the traveling palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the inner guard, 200 blocking Heavenly Martial officers and rank-and-file were assigned from experienced men of good conduct; they operated from outside the Xuande Gate to the traveling palace gate.

sentences.zh: 南渡後，乘輿出入，初未有儀。

translations.literal: After the southward crossing, when the palanquin went out and in, at first there were no regulations.
translations.idiomatic: After the southward crossing, the imperial palanquin initially had no fixed ceremonial protocol.

sentences.zh: 高宗將迎韋太后於郊，因製常行儀仗，用黃麾仗二千二百六十五人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong was about to welcome Empress Dowager Wei at the suburbs, he therefore established routine traveling ceremonial regalia, using the yellow-command guard of two thousand two hundred sixty-five men.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong prepared to welcome Empress Dowager Wei at the suburbs, he established routine traveling ceremonial regalia using 2,265 men of the yellow-command guard.

sentences.zh: 孝宗朝德壽宮，減一千人，用殿前司六百二十九人，皇城在內巡檢司三百九十一人，崇政殿四百四十九人，凡一千四百六十九人。

translations.literal: At Deshou Palace during Emperor Xiaozong's reign, one thousand men were reduced; six hundred twenty-nine from the Bureau of the Palatial Guard were used, three hundred ninety-one from the Imperial City Inner Inspection Command, four hundred forty-nine from Chongzheng Hall—in all one thousand four hundred sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: At Deshou Palace under Emperor Xiaozong, the escort was reduced by 1,000: 629 from the Palatial Guard, 391 from the Imperial City Inner Inspection Command, and 449 from Chongzheng Hall—1,469 in all.

sentences.zh: 四孟詣景靈宮，用殿前司八百七十五人，皇城在內巡檢司五百二十八人，崇政殿五百二十一人，凡一千九百二十四人。

translations.literal: For the four seasonal visits to Jingling Palace, eight hundred seventy-five from the Bureau of the Palatial Guard were used, five hundred twenty-eight from the Imperial City Inner Inspection Command, five hundred twenty-one from Chongzheng Hall—in all one thousand nine hundred twenty-four.
translations.idiomatic: For the four seasonal visits to Jingling Palace, the escort numbered 1,924: 875 from the Palatial Guard, 528 from the Imperial City Inner Inspection Command, and 521 from Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 九年正月，詔：駕出禦後殿坐，宰執、百官、儀衛等赴後殿，起居殿上；

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year, an edict stated: when the carriage went out, the emperor took his seat in the Rear Hall; the chief counselors, all officials, ceremonial guards, and the like went to the Rear Hall and performed obeisance in the upper hall;
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 9, an edict ordered: when the emperor departed, he first took his seat in the Rear Hall; chief counselors, officials, and ceremonial guards went to the Rear Hall and performed obeisance in the upper hall;

sentences.zh: 登輦，出後殿門，駕回，入祥曦殿門。

translations.literal: He mounted the palanquin, exited the Rear Hall gate; when the carriage returned, it entered through the Xiangxi Hall gate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mounted the palanquin and left through the Rear Hall gate; on return, the procession entered through the Xiangxi Hall gate.

sentences.zh: 太上皇儀衛。

translations.literal: Retired Emperor ceremonial guards.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial Guards for the Retired Emperor.

sentences.zh: 隆興元年，孝宗嗣位，詔有司討論德壽宮輿輦儀衛。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longxing, when Emperor Xiaozong succeeded to the throne, an edict ordered the relevant offices to discuss the palanquin and carriage ceremonial guards for Deshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In Longxing 1, when Emperor Xiaozong ascended the throne, the relevant offices were ordered to draft ceremonial protocols for the retired emperor's palanquin at Deshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 先是，紹興三十二年六月，詔：“上皇日常朝殿，差禦龍直四十三人，執仗排立，並設傘扇，鳴鞭。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the sixth month of the thirty-second year of Shaoxing, an edict stated: "For the Retired Emperor's daily audience in the hall, forty-three Imperial Dragon Direct were detailed, bearing weapons and standing in ranks, with parasols and fans set out and the whip sounded.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the sixth month of Shaoxing 32, an edict stated: "For the Retired Emperor's daily audience, detail forty-three Imperial Dragon Direct to stand in ranks bearing weapons, with parasols and fans deployed and the ceremonial whip sounded.

sentences.zh: 宰執退朝，仍赴德壽宮起居。

translations.literal: When the chief counselors left court, they still went to Deshou Palace to perform obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving court, chief counselors still went to Deshou Palace to pay their respects.

sentences.zh: 如遇行幸，令禁衛所隨以祗應。

translations.literal: If an imperial tour occurred, the Inner Guard Office was ordered to attend accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial tours, the Inner Guard Office was to provide appropriate escort.

sentences.zh: ”兩奉上皇旨，卻而不受，故復有是詔。

translations.literal: " Twice the edict was presented to the Retired Emperor, and twice he declined it, and so this edict was issued again.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor declined twice, which led to this renewed edict.

sentences.zh: 尋有司上言：“漢之未央，唐之興慶，其車輦儀衛不載。

translations.literal: Soon the relevant offices memorialized: "At Han's Weiyang and Tang's Xingqing, their carriage and palanquin ceremonial guards were not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Soon officials memorialized: "Neither Han's Weiyang Palace nor Tang's Xingqing Palace recorded protocols for carriage and palanquin ceremonial guards.

sentences.zh: 今父堯子舜，事親典禮，凡往古來今所未備者，當以義起，極其尊崇，為萬世法。

translations.literal: Now, with a father as Yao and a son as Shun, the rites of honoring parents—wherever past and present had not provided for them—should be initiated according to principle, carried to the utmost honor, and made a law for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: With a filial son like Shun honoring a sage father like Yao, rites not provided for in past or present should be established on principle, carried to the highest honor, and made a model for all time.

sentences.zh: ”遂定宰執、百官詣德壽宮起居，則禁衛所依後殿坐儀排列，禁衛二百九十七人祗應。

translations.literal: " It was then fixed that when chief counselors and all officials went to Deshou Palace to perform obeisance, the Inner Guard Office arranged them according to the Rear Hall seating ceremony, with two hundred ninety-seven inner guards attending.
translations.idiomatic: It was decided that when chief counselors and officials paid respects at Deshou Palace, the Inner Guard Office would array them according to the Rear Hall seating protocol, with 297 inner guards in attendance.

sentences.zh: 行幸，則禁衛所差行門、禁衛諸班直、天武親從官及傘扇、鳴鞭、燭罩等合五百人，隨行扈從。

translations.literal: On imperial tours, the Inner Guard Office detailed gate guides, various inner-guard duty shifts, Heavenly Martial personal followers, and parasols, fans, whip, and candle shades—in all five hundred men—to escort and attend.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial tours, the Inner Guard Office detailed 500 men—gate guides, various guard duty shifts, Heavenly Martial personal followers, plus parasols, fans, ceremonial whip, and candle shades—to escort the retired emperor.

sentences.zh: 前引七十人：內行宮殿前崇政殿親從一十人，都下親從二十人，快行親從二十人，殿前指揮使二十人。

translations.literal: Seventy men in the forward escort: ten personal followers of Chongzheng Hall at the traveling palace forecourt; twenty personal followers of the capital; twenty fast-march personal followers; twenty Palatial Guard commanders.
translations.idiomatic: The forward escort numbered 70: ten Chongzheng Hall personal followers at the traveling palace forecourt, twenty capital personal followers, twenty fast-march personal followers, and twenty Palatial Guard commanders.

sentences.zh: 中道六十人：編排禁衛行子一十人，執從物禦龍直三十人，執傘扇天武一十人，崇政殿親從攔前一十人。

translations.literal: Sixty men in the central route: ten inner-guard route marshals; thirty Imperial Dragon Direct bearing attendant objects; ten Heavenly Martial bearing parasols and fans; ten Chongzheng Hall personal followers blocking in front.
translations.idiomatic: The central route numbered 60: ten inner-guard route marshals, thirty Imperial Dragon Direct bearing attendant objects, ten Heavenly Martial with parasols and fans, and ten Chongzheng Hall personal followers posted in front.

sentences.zh: 禁衛圍子四重四百人：第一，崇政殿親從一百人；

translations.literal: Four layers of inner-guard escort ring, four hundred men: first, one hundred Chongzheng Hall personal followers;
translations.idiomatic: The inner-guard escort ring had four layers totaling 400: first, 100 Chongzheng Hall personal followers;

sentences.zh: 第二，禦龍直、骨朵直、弓箭直三十人，東西班七十人；

translations.literal: Second, thirty Imperial Dragon Direct, geku Direct, and bow Direct; seventy east and west companies;
translations.idiomatic: Second, 30 Imperial Dragon Direct, geku Direct, and bow Direct, plus 70 east and west companies;

sentences.zh: 第三，執燭罩都下親從一百人；

translations.literal: Third, one hundred capital personal followers bearing candle shades;
translations.idiomatic: Third, 100 capital personal followers bearing candle shades;

sentences.zh: 第四，內殿直一十人，散員、散指揮、散都頭、散祗候、金鎗、銀鎗班各一十人，後從殿前指揮使二十人。

translations.literal: Fourth, ten Inner Palace Direct; ten each from scattered members, scattered commanders, scattered company heads, scattered attendants, golden spear, and silver spear companies; twenty Palatial Guard commanders following behind.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, ten Inner Palace Direct; ten each from scattered members, commanders, company heads, attendants, golden spear, and silver spear companies; and twenty Palatial Guard commanders at the rear.

sentences.zh: 皇太后儀衛。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager ceremonial guards.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial Guards for the Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 自乾興元年仁宗即位，章獻太后預政，侍衛始盛。

translations.literal: From the first year of Qianxing, when Emperor Renzong ascended the throne and Empress Dowager Zhangxian participated in government, the escort guards first flourished.
translations.idiomatic: From Qianxing 1, when Emperor Renzong ascended the throne and Empress Dowager Zhangxian shared in governance, empress dowager escorts first reached full scale.

sentences.zh: 用禮儀院奏，製皇太后所乘輿，名之曰“大安輦”。

translations.literal: Following the Ceremonial Institute's memorial, the palanquin ridden by the Empress Dowager was made and named the "Grand Peace Palanquin."
translations.idiomatic: On the Ceremonial Institute's recommendation, the empress dowager's palanquin was created and named the Grand Peace Palanquin.

sentences.zh: 天聖元年，有司言：“皇太后車駕出，合設護衛：禦龍直都虞候一人，都頭二人，副都頭一人，十將、長行五十人十將已下；

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiansheng, the relevant offices stated: "When the Empress Dowager's carriage went out, escort guards should be provided: one Imperial Dragon Direct chief commander, two company heads, one deputy company head, fifty squad leaders and rank-and-file down to squad leaders;
translations.idiomatic: In Tiansheng 1, officials reported: "When the empress dowager's carriage departed, the following escort should be provided: one Imperial Dragon Direct chief commander, two company heads, one deputy company head, and fifty men including squad leaders and rank-and-file;

sentences.zh: 骨朵子直都虞候一人，都頭二人，副都頭二人，十將、長行八十人；

translations.literal: One geku Direct chief commander, two company heads, two deputy company heads, eighty squad leaders and rank-and-file;
translations.idiomatic: one geku Direct chief commander, two company heads, two deputy company heads, and eighty squad leaders and rank-and-file;

sentences.zh: 弓箭直指揮使一人，都頭二人，副都頭二人，十將、長行五十人；

translations.literal: One bow Direct commander, two company heads, two deputy company heads, fifty squad leaders and rank-and-file;
translations.idiomatic: one bow Direct commander, two company heads, two deputy company heads, and fifty squad leaders and rank-and-file;

sentences.zh: 弩直指揮使一人，都頭二人，副都頭二人，十將、長行五十人。

translations.literal: One crossbow Direct commander, two company heads, two deputy company heads, fifty squad leaders and rank-and-file.
translations.idiomatic: and one crossbow Direct commander, two company heads, two deputy company heads, and fifty squad leaders and rank-and-file.

sentences.zh: 殿前指揮使兩班：左班都虞候一人，都知一人，行門三人，長行二十人，帶器械；

translations.literal: Two companies of Palatial Guard commanders: left company one chief commander, one chief steward, three gate guides, twenty rank-and-file, bearing weapons;
translations.idiomatic: Two Palatial Guard companies: the left company—one chief commander, one chief steward, three gate guides, twenty rank-and-file, all armed;

sentences.zh: 右班指揮使一人，都知一人，行門三人，長行二十人，帶器械。

translations.literal: Right company one commander, one chief steward, three gate guides, twenty rank-and-file, bearing weapons.
translations.idiomatic: the right company—one commander, one chief steward, three gate guides, twenty rank-and-file, all armed.

sentences.zh: 皇城司禁衛二百人，寬衣天武二百人，供禦輦官六十二人，寬衣天武百人。

translations.literal: Two hundred inner guards of the Imperial City Command, two hundred broad-garment Heavenly Martial, sixty-two palanquin attendants for the imperial palanquin, one hundred broad-garment Heavenly Martial.
translations.idiomatic: 200 Imperial City inner guards, 200 broad-garment Heavenly Martial, 62 attendants for the imperial palanquin, and 100 broad-garment Heavenly Martial.

sentences.zh: 餘諸司祗應、鳴鞭、侍衛，如乘輿之儀。

translations.literal: The remaining attendants of the various bureaus, whip-sounding, and escort guards followed the ceremony for the imperial palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: Other bureau attendants, ceremonial whip, and escort guards followed the same protocol as for the imperial palanquin.

sentences.zh: ”詔依。

translations.literal: " An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 治平元年，詔皇太后出入唯不鳴鞭，他儀衛如章獻明肅故事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhiping, an edict stated that when the Empress Dowager went out and in, only the sounding of the whip was omitted; other ceremonial guards followed the precedents of Empress Dowager Zhangxian Mingsu.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiping 1, an edict held that the empress dowager's processions omitted only the ceremonial whip; all other guards followed Empress Dowager Zhangxian Mingsu's precedents.

sentences.zh: 四年，神宗嗣位，詔太皇太后儀範已定，皇太后合設儀衛：禦龍直、骨朵子直差都虞候、都頭、副都頭各一人，十將、長行各共三十人；

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when Emperor Shenzong succeeded to the throne, an edict stated that the Grand Empress Dowager's protocol was already fixed, and the Empress Dowager should have ceremonial guards provided: Imperial Dragon Direct and geku Direct each detailed one chief commander, one company head, and one deputy company head, with thirty squad leaders and rank-and-file in all;
translations.idiomatic: In year 4, when Emperor Shenzong succeeded, an edict noted that the grand empress dowager's protocol was already fixed and ordered ceremonial guards for the empress dowager: Imperial Dragon Direct and geku Direct each with one chief commander, one company head, one deputy company head, and 30 squad leaders and rank-and-file;

sentences.zh: 弓箭直、弩直差指揮使、都頭、副都頭各一人，十將、長行各共二十人。

translations.literal: Bow Direct and crossbow Direct each detailed one commander, one company head, and one deputy company head, with twenty squad leaders and rank-and-file in all.
translations.idiomatic: bow Direct and crossbow Direct each with one commander, one company head, one deputy company head, and 20 squad leaders and rank-and-file.

sentences.zh: 皇城司親從官一百人，執骨朵寬衣天武官百五十人，充圍子行宮司人員共一百人，入內院子五十人，充圍子皇城司親事官八十人。

translations.literal: One hundred personal followers of the Imperial City Command, one hundred fifty broad-garment Heavenly Martial officers bearing geku, one hundred Traveling Palace Command officers serving as the escort ring; fifty Inner Palace Courtyard personnel; eighty Imperial City Command attendants serving as the escort ring.
translations.idiomatic: 100 Imperial City personal followers, 150 broad-garment Heavenly Martial officers with geku, 100 Traveling Palace Command officers in the escort ring, 50 Inner Palace Courtyard personnel, and 80 Imperial City attendants in the escort ring.

sentences.zh: 打燈籠、短鐙馬、攏馬親從官，金銅車、棕車隨車子祗應人，擎擔子供禦輦官，執擎從物等供禦、次供禦並下都輦直等，人數不定。

translations.literal: Lantern bearers, short-stirrup horses, horse-gathering personal followers, attendants for golden-bronze and palm-fiber carts following the carts, palanquin attendants bearing carrying poles for the imperial palanquin, attendants bearing attendant objects including primary attendants, secondary attendants, and Capital Palanquin Direct—the numbers were not fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Lantern bearers, short-stirrup horses, horse-gathering personal followers, attendants for golden-bronze and palm-fiber carts, pole-bearing palanquin attendants, attendants for attendant objects including primary and secondary attendants and Capital Palanquin Direct—the numbers were unfixed.

sentences.zh: 都知一員，禦藥院使臣二員，內東門司使臣二員，內酒坊、禦廚、法酒庫、儀鸞司、乳酪院、翰林司、翰林院、車子院、禦膳素廚、化成殿果子庫，並從。

translations.literal: One chief steward, two Imperial Pharmacy envoys, two Inner East Gate Command envoys, and the Inner Wine Workshop, Imperial Kitchen, Legal Wine Storehouse, Ceremonial Parasol Office, Dairy Office, Hanlin Secretariat, Hanlin Academy, Cart Office, Imperial Vegetarian Kitchen, and Huacheng Hall Fruit Storehouse—all followed.
translations.idiomatic: One chief steward, two Imperial Pharmacy envoys, two Inner East Gate envoys, and the Inner Wine Workshop, Imperial Kitchen, Legal Wine Storehouse, Ceremonial Parasol Office, Dairy Office, Hanlin Secretariat, Hanlin Academy, Cart Office, Imperial Vegetarian Kitchen, and Huacheng Hall Fruit Storehouse—all accompanied the procession.

sentences.zh: 遇出新城門，添差帶器械內臣。

translations.literal: When exiting the New City Gate, inner attendants bearing weapons were additionally assigned.
translations.idiomatic: When leaving through the New City Gate, armed inner attendants were additionally assigned.

sentences.zh: 仁、英、哲之世，太后臨朝垂簾，儀從亦不崇侈，止曰儀衛，無鹵薄名也。

translations.literal: In the eras of Ren, Ying, and Zhe, when empress dowagers attended court behind the curtain, their escorts were also not lavishly expanded; they were only called ceremonial guards, without the name of imperial procession regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperors Ren, Ying, and Zhe, when empress dowagers presided from behind the curtain, their escorts were kept modest—called ceremonial guards only, never granted the title of full imperial procession regalia.

sentences.zh: 南渡後尤簡，其車以輿不以輦，餘惟傘、扇而已。

translations.literal: After the southward crossing they were especially simplified: their conveyance was a palanquin carriage rather than an imperial palanquin; beyond that only parasols and fans.
translations.idiomatic: After the southward crossing, escorts were simplified further: empress dowagers rode in palanquin carriages rather than imperial palanquins, with nothing beyond parasols and fans.

sentences.zh: 紹興奉迎太母，極意備禮，然猶曰太后天性樸素，不敢過飾儀從。

translations.literal: When Shaoxing welcomed the Grand Empress Dowager, they prepared rites to the utmost, yet still said the empress dowager's nature was plain and simple and they dared not over-adorn the escort.
translations.idiomatic: During Shaoxing's welcome of the Grand Empress Dowager, every effort was made to observe full protocol, yet officials noted her plain nature and dared not over-adorn her escort.

sentences.zh: 器物惟塗金，輿前用黃羅傘扇二，緋黃繡雉扇六，紅黃緋金拂扇二，黃羅暖扇二。

translations.literal: Objects were only gold-plated; before the palanquin two yellow-silk parasol-fans were used, six scarlet-yellow embroidered pheasant-tail fans, two red-yellow scarlet gold whisk fans, and two yellow-silk warming fans.
translations.idiomatic: Regalia was gold-plated only; before the palanquin were two yellow-silk parasol-fans, six scarlet-yellow embroidered pheasant-tail fans, two red-yellow scarlet gold whisk fans, and two yellow-silk warming fans.

sentences.zh: 朝謁景靈宮、太廟，則用禁衛諸班直、天武親從五百人。

translations.literal: When paying court at Jingling Palace and the Imperial Ancestral Temple, five hundred from various inner-guard duty shifts and Heavenly Martial personal followers were used.
translations.idiomatic: For audiences at Jingling Palace and the Imperial Ancestral Temple, 500 men from various inner-guard duty shifts and Heavenly Martial personal followers were deployed.

sentences.zh: 其前引、中道、圍子，同上皇儀衛而差省焉。

translations.literal: The forward escort, central route, and escort ring followed the retired emperor's ceremonial guards but with reductions.
translations.idiomatic: The forward escort, central route, and escort ring followed the retired emperor's protocol but in reduced numbers.

sentences.zh: 二年，臣僚又言：“元符皇后，元符末嚐預定策之勳，以承神宗、哲宗之誌。

translations.literal: In the second year, officials again stated: "Empress Yuanfu, at the end of the Yuanfu era, had once shared in the merit of settling the succession, bearing the intentions of Emperors Shenzong and Zhezong.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2, officials again memorialized: "Empress Yuanfu, at the end of the Yuanfu era, had shared in settling the succession and carried forward the intentions of Emperors Shenzong and Zhezong.

sentences.zh: ”禮部太常寺奏：“典禮，準聖瑞皇太妃例，侍從官入內內侍省都知或押班一員，皇城、禦藥、內東門司官各一員，禦輦院輪官隨從，諸司禦燎子、茶床、帶禦器械內侍十人，引喝內侍一人。

translations.literal: " The Ministry of Rites and Court of Imperial Sacrifices memorialized: "According to ritual, following the precedent of Sacred Auspice Imperial Consort, escort officials included: one chief steward or ushership leader of the Inner Service entering the inner palace; one official each from the Imperial City, Imperial Pharmacy, and Inner East Gate Commands; a rotating official from the Imperial Palanquin Office to follow; ten inner attendants with imperial braziers, tea tables, and imperial weapons from various bureaus; one inner attendant to lead and announce.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites and Court of Imperial Sacrifices replied: "Following the precedent of Sacred Auspice Imperial Consort, escort officials should include one chief steward or ushership leader of the Inner Service, one official each from the Imperial City, Imperial Pharmacy, and Inner East Gate Commands, a rotating official from the Imperial Palanquin Office, ten inner attendants with imperial braziers, tea tables, and weapons, and one herald.

sentences.zh: 輿用龍鳳，傘紅黃兼用。

translations.literal: The palanquin used dragon-and-phoenix decoration; parasols used both red and yellow.
translations.idiomatic: The palanquin bore dragon-and-phoenix decoration; parasols were red and yellow.

sentences.zh: 出入由宣德東門，今欲出入由宣德正門。

translations.literal: Entry and exit was through the Xuande East Gate; now it was desired to enter and exit through the Xuande main gate.
translations.idiomatic: Entry and exit had been through the Xuande East Gate; now the request was to use the Xuande main gate.

sentences.zh: 龍鳳扇二十柄，今添作三十柄。

translations.literal: Twenty dragon-and-phoenix fans; now to add to thirty.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon-and-phoenix fans were increased from twenty to thirty.

sentences.zh: 輦官供禦六十二人，次供禦四十九人，都下五十八人。

translations.literal: Palanquin attendants: sixty-two primary attendants, forty-nine secondary attendants, fifty-eight capital attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Palanquin attendants: 62 primary attendants, 49 secondary attendants, and 58 capital attendants.

sentences.zh: 禦龍直三十三人，今添作四十五人。

translations.literal: Imperial Dragon Direct thirty-three men; now to add to forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Dragon Direct was increased from 33 to 45.

sentences.zh: 禦龍骨朵子直三十三人，今添作五十人。

translations.literal: Imperial Dragon geku Direct thirty-three men; now to add to fifty.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Dragon geku Direct was increased from 33 to 50.

sentences.zh: 禦龍弓箭直三十三人，今添作四十五人。

translations.literal: Imperial Dragon bow Direct thirty-three men; now to add to forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Dragon bow Direct was increased from 33 to 45.

sentences.zh: 禦龍弩直二十三人，今添作四十五人。

translations.literal: Imperial Dragon crossbow Direct twenty-three men; now to add to forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Dragon crossbow Direct was increased from 23 to 45.

sentences.zh: 殿前指揮三十二人，今添作四十五人。

translations.literal: Palatial Guard command thirty-two men; now to add to forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Palatial Guard command was increased from 32 to 45.

sentences.zh: 內臣二人。

translations.literal: Two inner attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Two inner attendants were assigned.

sentences.zh: 皇城司一百人禁衛，今添作一百二十人。

translations.literal: One hundred inner guards of the Imperial City Command; now to add to one hundred twenty.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial City inner guards were increased from 100 to 120.

sentences.zh: 天武官一百五十四人，行宮司一百人，入內院子五十人。

translations.literal: One hundred fifty-four Heavenly Martial officers, one hundred Traveling Palace Command personnel, fifty Inner Palace Courtyard personnel.
translations.idiomatic: 154 Heavenly Martial officers, 100 Traveling Palace Command personnel, and 50 Inner Palace Courtyard personnel.

sentences.zh: 快行親從官四人，今添作八人。

translations.literal: Four fast-march personal follower officers; now to add to eight.
translations.idiomatic: Fast-march personal followers were increased from 4 to 8.

sentences.zh: 執燭、皇城司親從官、金銅車並棕車，逐時內中批出合要數供須。

translations.literal: Candle bearers, Imperial City personal followers, golden-bronze and palm-fiber carts—as needed, numbers were approved and issued from within the palace at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Candle bearers, Imperial City personal followers, and golden-bronze and palm-fiber carts were supplied in whatever numbers the palace approved at the time.

sentences.zh: 行幸藥架一坐，勾當官一員，吏人二員，封題一員，藥童三人，抬檠藥架輦官十一人，秤、庫子親事官，量差人數祗應。

translations.literal: One traveling medicine stand; one supervising official, two clerks, one seal-and-label official, three medicine boys, eleven palanquin attendants to carry the medicine stand, scale and storehouse attendants—in numbers assigned as needed to attend.
translations.idiomatic: One traveling medicine stand with one supervising official, two clerks, one seal-and-label official, three medicine boys, eleven palanquin attendants to carry the stand, plus scale and storehouse attendants in numbers as needed.

sentences.zh: ”從之。

translations.literal: " It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 皇后儀衛，惟東都《政和禮》有鹵簿，他無鹵簿之名，惟曰儀衛而已。

translations.literal: Empress ceremonial guards: only the Eastern Capital's "Zhenghe Rites" had imperial procession regalia; elsewhere there was no name of procession regalia, only ceremonial guards.
translations.idiomatic: For the empress, only the Eastern Capital's 《Ceremonial Standards of the Zhenghe Era》 recorded full imperial procession regalia; elsewhere the title was never used—only ceremonial guards.

sentences.zh: 中興後，皇太后既尚簡素，後尤簡焉。

translations.literal: After the Restoration, since the Empress Dowager already valued simplicity, the empress was even more simplified.
translations.idiomatic: After the Restoration, with the empress dowager already favoring simplicity, the empress's escort was simplified still further.

sentences.zh: 出入朝謁宮廟，用應奉禦輦官一員，人吏三人。

translations.literal: Going out and in for court audiences at palaces and temples, one Palace Service imperial palanquin attendant and three clerks were used.
translations.idiomatic: For audiences at palaces and temples, one Palace Service imperial palanquin attendant and three clerks sufficed.

sentences.zh: 供應六十三人：內人員十五人，頭帽、紫羅四衤癸單衫、金塗銀柘枝腰帶；

translations.literal: Primary attendants sixty-three men: fifteen officers within, head caps, purple silk cross-collared single tunics, gold-plated silver branch waist belts;
translations.idiomatic: Primary attendants numbered 63: 15 officers wearing head caps, purple silk cross-collared tunics, and gold-plated silver branch belts;

sentences.zh: 肩擎輦官四十八人，襆頭、緋羅單衫、金塗海捷腰帶、紫羅表夾三襜、緋羅看帶。

translations.literal: Forty-eight shoulder-bearing palanquin attendants, black caps, scarlet silk single tunics, gold-plated sea-quick waist belts, purple silk outer lined triple-apron coats, scarlet silk viewing sashes.
translations.idiomatic: 48 shoulder-bearing palanquin attendants in black caps, scarlet silk tunics, gold-plated sea-quick belts, purple silk outer lined triple-apron coats, and scarlet viewing sashes.

sentences.zh: 次供應十四人：內人員一人，服同上，惟海捷帶；

translations.literal: Secondary attendants fourteen men: one officer within, dress the same as above, only sea-quick belt;
translations.idiomatic: Secondary attendants numbered 14: one officer in the same dress as above but with a sea-quick belt;

sentences.zh: 輦官一十三人，服同肩擎官，惟行獅帶。

translations.literal: Thirteen palanquin attendants, dress the same as shoulder-bearers, only lion-pattern belt.
translations.idiomatic: 13 palanquin attendants in the same dress as shoulder-bearers but with lion-pattern belts.

sentences.zh: 都下五十四人：內人員一人，帽服同前；

translations.literal: Capital attendants fifty-four men: one officer within, cap and dress the same as before;
translations.idiomatic: Capital attendants numbered 54: one officer in the same cap and dress as above;

sentences.zh: 輦官五十三人，服同上，輦宮惟云鶴帶。

translations.literal: Fifty-three palanquin attendants, dress the same as above; for palanquin attendants only cloud-crane belt.
translations.idiomatic: 53 palanquin attendants in the same dress, with cloud-crane belts only.
